ideas.title: Narrative is the recurrent first-visible point of pipeline drift — focus trials and controls there
ideas.description: The report shows the Narrative stage is the most frequent earliest observable break in the requested company-first editorial hierarchy. Treating Narrative as a primary locus for diagnostic intervention (instead of only changing Idea or Compose) offers the clearest, source-supported opportunity to preserve a company-first introduction while keeping product details as supporting context.
ideas.audience: Content experiment designers, prompt engineers, editorial leads and workflow owners running Nuëyon.Compose pipeline experiments.
ideas.rationale: Why it matters: Experiment traceability across 007–009 repeatedly localizes first visible hierarchy shifts to Narrative (e.g., 007 runs 001–002; 008 A-002; 009 baseline 002/003 and candidates 001–003). The same experiments also show that a company-first Idea can be selected yet be reframed downstream, so upstream Idea changes alone are insufficient. Focusing a controlled trial on Narrative (with fixed upstream inputs) minimizes confounding sources and directly tests whether Narrative-stage conditioning or prompt wording is allowing product- or orchestration-led reframing. Gaps & uncertainty: Narrative is the most recurrent visible locus but not the sole origin — some runs start in Idea or Synthesis — so a Narrative-only fix may not address all failure modes.
ideas.evidence: Executive findings and 'First observable drift by run' tables: the report states 'Narrative is the most recurrent first visible hierarchy shift' and lists concrete runs where Narrative is first (Experiment 007 candidates 001–002; Experiment 008 A-002; Experiment 009 baseline 002/003 and candidates 001–003). It also records runs where Idea or Synthesis initiated drift (e.g., 008 A-001, 007 candidate 003), supporting the qualification that Narrative is recurrent but not sole.

ideas.title: Upstream format leakage plausibly primes downstream scope and phrasing — remove format cues from Idea/Research/Narrative prompts
ideas.description: The Master Workflow intends upstream stages to be format-independent, but the frozen prompts include explicit format references (Article, LinkedIn, etc.). That leakage is a credible source of priming that may influence story selection and phrasing later in Narrative and Compose; removing these format cues upstream is a focused editorial opportunity to reduce unintended priming.
ideas.audience: Prompt engineers, workflow architects, and teams responsible for Master Workflow and prompt governance.
ideas.rationale: Why it matters: The architecture audit found direct format references in Idea, Research, and Narrative system/user prompts even though the Master Workflow requires format-independence. Removing or isolating those references clarifies role boundaries and reduces a plausible source of upstream priming. Gaps & uncertainty: The report explicitly states this is an 'instruction-boundary inconsistency' and that format references are a 'plausible source of format priming' but does not prove causation between these prompt references and specific hierarchy drifts.
ideas.evidence: Format-agnostic architecture audit: 'Frozen Idea system prompt includes “supported output formats”...', 'Frozen Research system prompt also lists “an article writer”...', and 'Frozen Narrative system prompt ... names articles, LinkedIn posts, newsletters...' The report also states the Master Workflow says upstream agents should remain format-independent.

ideas.title: A company-first Idea is necessary but not sufficient — add cross-stage integrity checks to preserve story priority
ideas.description: Experiment 009 demonstrates that selecting a company-first Idea did not prevent downstream reframing (orchestration-centered story, unsupported audience/validation language). The editorial opportunity is to introduce integrity checks that validate the company-first hierarchy and scope at Synthesis, Narrative and Compose, not only at Idea selection.
ideas.audience: Experiment evaluators, editorial QA teams, and product-story owners who must ensure consistent messaging across pipeline stages.
ideas.rationale: Why it matters: The evidence shows correct upstream selection can still yield a product-first final output; therefore, gating or lightweight checks at subsequent stages (Synthesis, Narrative, Compose) would catch reframe or factual-strengthening regressions before Compose finalizes messaging. Gaps & uncertainty: The report documents where drift occurs but does not prescribe exact gating mechanisms; the appropriate gate design and acceptance criteria remain to be defined and tested.
ideas.evidence: Executive findings point 3: 'a company-first selected Idea is not sufficient' — Experiment 009 kept Nuëyon primary in Ideas but downstream outputs showed orchestration-centered framing and unsupported claims. Cross-experiment patterns also state 'All selected Ideas can look company-first while Narrative/Compose later reframe the story.'

ideas.title: Design a controlled upstream-boundary trial that targets Narrative and measures both fidelity and editorial quality
ideas.description: The report recommends a single controlled experiment that (a) targets the stage with the strongest evidence for first failure (Narrative), (b) preserves the company-first subject/product relationship, (c) isolates format-awareness changes, and (d) separately evaluates factual integrity, hierarchy fidelity, and editorial quality. Running repeated full-pipeline comparisons with these constraints is a clear next editorial experiment.
ideas.audience: Research designers, experiment operators, and QA/evaluation teams running Nuëyon.Compose experiments.
ideas.rationale: Why it matters: The report’s 'Implication for the next focused trial' section enumerates these trial elements as the next useful diagnostic step. A controlled trial built from that prescription can more confidently localize causes and avoid confounding changes across prompts. Gaps & uncertainty: The report provides the trial specification but not empirical outcomes — the trial itself must be executed to confirm whether Narrative or other factors are causal.
ideas.evidence: Implication for the next focused trial: the report explicitly lists a five-point controlled-trial plan (target Narrative, preserve company/product relationship, manage format reasoning, use repeated runs and identical settings, and evaluate three separate axes). It also notes previous experiments (007–009) demonstrated mixed origins of drift, motivating this controlled approach.

ideas.title: Editorial quality (hook, readability, narrative progression) is under-measured — add engagement-focused criteria alongside factual checks
ideas.description: Current evaluations emphasize factuality and hierarchy but do not consistently measure opening impact, readability, or memorability. The report flags this as a distinct shortcoming and an editorial opportunity: add consistent editorial-quality metrics so a surviving company-first framing is also compelling.
ideas.audience: Content evaluators, editorial reviewers, product marketing leads and experiment scoring teams.
ideas.rationale: Why it matters: The report observes that outputs can be source-aligned yet weakly engaging (process descriptions, architecture lists, or repetitive framing). Without consistent editorial metrics, runs that pass fidelity checks may still fail to produce usable, attention-grabbing company introductions. Gaps & uncertainty: The report identifies the measurement gap but does not define specific metric thresholds or tooling — implementing meaningful editorial metrics requires further design and alignment on what 'compelling' means in this context.
ideas.evidence: Executive findings point 5 and Cross-experiment patterns: 'The outputs are not consistently strong LinkedIn editorial content even when broadly source-aligned' and 'Engagement has been under-measured... Earlier run evaluations mainly score factuality, hierarchy, and condition fidelity.'
